item.title: In 2016, conservationists put the bends back into a Lake District river straightened 200 years earlier
item.description: Conservationists undertook an inspiring project to restore the natural meanders of Swindale Beck, which had been straightened for centuries. Within just a few months, the restored gravel beds welcomed back the Atlantic salmon to spawn, while also decreasing flood risks and enhancing drinking water quality for millions. This remarkable recovery fostered a thriving habitat for aquatic insects and river birds, ultimately earning the UK River Prize in 2022.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: MrBeast reacts as viral Terraria kid reveals heartbreaking reason behind pause in Terraria videos
item.description: In a heartfelt announcement, Instagram creator michaelshowscoolthings shared that he will be taking a break from his engaging Terraria content due to his family’s unexpected financial strains and an upcoming move. This tough personal ordeal has led him to reassess his priorities. MrBeast, the renowned YouTube star, reached out with uplifting words to help the young creator navigate through this challenging chapter.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: 5 insane Twitch records that may be nearly impossible for another streamer to break
item.description: Twitch has seen some unbelievable milestones, but five records stand far above the rest. Ibai Llanos reached more than 9.3 million peak viewers, Kai Cenat crossed 1.1 million active subscribers, and Neuro-sama hit Level 126 on a Hype Train. TheGrefg’s Fortnite reveal reached 2.47 million viewers, while Ludwig’s month-long subathon created an endurance benchmark that remains extremely difficult to extend further.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Khamzat Chimaev accepts surprising fight offer from top UFC contender after losing middleweight title
item.description: In a bold move, Caio Borralho has issued a challenge to Khamzat Chimaev for a prospective fight, proposing two dates in November and December. After losing his middleweight title, Chimaev is weighing his options. This clash could play a pivotal role in shaping the future of the middleweight division, with Borralho ranked sixth and Chimaev ranked twelfth globally.

item.title: In 2020, Ohio removed a dam from the once-polluted Cuyahoga River; it reopened 39 km of habitat
item.description: The removal of the Brecksville Diversion Dam has enhanced river habitats, allowing migrating fish to thrive. Researchers documented the arrival of fifteen new fish species within the lower Cuyahoga River. While native species have successfully reestablished their presence, the advent of nonnative species also marked a significant change in the ecosystem. Ongoing efforts to eliminate more dams aim to further rejuvenate the Cuyahoga River basin for future generations.

item.title: At 15, Jim Bishop bought 2.5 acres for $450; he spent 50 years building a castle that is world's largest one-man project
item.description: For over five decades, Jim Bishop dedicated his life to building the biggest one-man castle in the world, starting in 1969. His ambition was fueled by a determination to silence skeptics, initially using his own funds and later gathering donations. After Jim's passing in November 2024, his son Daniel has taken up the monumental task, ensuring the legacy of this extraordinary masterpiece lives on.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1967, astronaut Vance Brand bought 160 acres beside Rocky Mountain National Park for $32,000
item.description: In a generous act, former astronaut Vance Brand has gifted forty acres of land to Rocky Mountain National Park. This pristine, undeveloped forest area now forms part of the park's eastern boundary, following congressional legislation passed in 2021 to officially recognize the donation. Protecting popular hiking trails from potential development, this land also ensures the preservation of essential high-elevation ecosystems for the enjoyment of future generations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1964, a couple bought 535 acres in North Carolina and built a summer home there; decades later...
item.description: Transforming a cherished family haven into a hub for environmental research, this 535-acre property in North Carolina has been generously donated to the National Park Service. Now known as the Appalachian Highlands Science Learning Center, it plays a crucial role in studying the impacts of climate change and preserving the unique biodiversity of high-elevation ecosystems. Ongoing scientific investigations and educational initiatives thrive here, ensuring this legacy benefits future generations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Gloria Steinem dies at 92: Hillary Clinton, Meghan Markle, Lena Dunham pay tribute to feminist icon
item.description: Gloria Steinem, the pioneering feminist activist, author and journalist, has passed away at 92. Following her death, Hillary Clinton, Meghan Markle, Lena Dunham and others paid heartfelt tributes, remembering her influence, generosity and lifelong fight for equality. From women’s rights to reproductive freedom, Steinem’s work inspired generations and left an enduring mark on society.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nepal floods: No bodies to cremate, kin burn kusha effigies as hopes fade for missing
item.description: Families in Nuwakot and Rasuwa performed symbolic cremations for missing flood victims. Relatives used kusha grass effigies when bodies could not be recovered. Searches for missing kin proved unsuccessful across various locations. Priests guided families through traditional rituals for liberating souls. Over one hundred effigies were cremated in Kathmandu's Pashupati Aryaghat.
item.dc:creator: Vishant Agarwala

item.title: A Virginia mountaintop was scarred by coal mining; it now holds a 200,000-square-foot high school
item.description: In Buchanan County, Virginia, a state-of-the-art high school has been inaugurated on land reclaimed from mining activities. This new educational facility brings together four outdated schools into a single, modern campus. It provides a variety of academic and vocational options for students while aiming to lessen resource inequalities and promote local youth resilience, showcasing a major commitment to the community's development.

item.title: NBA legend Kevin Garnett’s former Malibu mansion listed for $48 million after massive makeover
item.description: NBA legend Kevin Garnett’s former Malibu mansion is now listed for $48 million after a major transformation. Garnett purchased the Pacific Coast Highway property for $6.4 million in 2003 and began building a custom home that remained unfinished. Following a failed $16 million sale and legal disputes, the estate was completed and transformed into a luxury residence.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: A dying mother’s wish protects 2,506 acres ranch
item.description: David Ellsbury honored his late mother's wish by safeguarding the family's cherished Diamond E Ranch from development. Spanning 2,506 acres, this land is now forever shielded by a land trust, ensuring that future generations can enjoy its unspoiled beauty. The ranching traditions of the family will thrive on this preserved estate.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 5 migrants dead after boat carrying over 100 people drifts for weeks in Atlantic
item.description: At least five African migrants died after their boat encountered trouble at sea. Forty-four survivors were rescued and brought to safety near Gran Canaria. Survivors reported being adrift for nearly a month without provisions. Many migrants suffered dehydration and illness after drinking seawater. The Atlantic route to the Canary Islands remains a dangerous journey.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Kodak retiree finds new animal in moss from New York log; scientists confirm it as a new tardigrade
item.description: A retired Kodak finance worker and longtime volunteer, Judy Dobles, discovered a previously unknown tardigrade species after collecting moss from a log at New York’s Cumming Nature Center and examining it under a microscope. The species was formally recognised about a year later. Named Mesocrista ojagwaji, it adds to the growing list of tardigrades identified in New York and highlights how much microscopic life remains to be studied.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
